The HTTP server: the serve command, run without arguments too, the routes with /healthz, graceful shutdown, and package edge, which every request goes through: a request ID, an access log, panics answered as 500, errors as Problem Details (RFC 9457), and not_found for unknown addresses. Other blueprints add routes and middleware.

```esquadro
blueprint http
```

## Works with

- **Requires** [app](../app/): the app must use them too.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `port` | int | `8080` | Port the server listens on; PORT overrides it. |
| `trust_proxy` | bool | `false` | Take the client's address from X-Forwarded-For, for the log and the rate limit; only behind a proxy that sets it. &lt;APP>_TRUST_PROXY overrides it. |

```esquadro
blueprint http {
  port 8080
}
```

## Environment variables

Read when the app starts; see [Environment variables](/esquadro/language/environment/).

| Variable | Type | Value | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | int | the port option | The port the HTTP server listens on. |
| `<APP>_TRUST_PROXY` | bool | the trust_proxy option | Take the client's address from X-Forwarded-For. |

## Slots

Other blueprints add code at these points (see [Writing a blueprint](/esquadro/writing-blueprints/#slots)).

| Slot | |
|---|---|
| `http.routes.imports` | Imports of cmd/&lt;app>/routes.go. |
| `http.routes` | Routes, registered on mux; d is the dependencies, and an error is returned as nil, err. |
| `http.middleware.context` | Middleware that sets the request's context before anything answers, one per line ending with a comma, e.g. edge.Localize,. |
| `http.middleware` | Middleware every request goes through, inside the access log and the panic recovery, one per line ending with a comma. |
| `http.problem.title` | Code in edge.DocumentOf that changes a problem's title for the request of ctx: title holds it, p is the problem. |
